newsitem.title: UK: Fixtures, new orders reported on sugar freight mkt.
newsitem.headline: Fixtures, new orders reported on sugar freight mkt.

text.p: London's sugar freight market saw a spate of fresh inquiry on Wednesday with a mixed bag of origins and destinations.
Commodity Specialists quoted for 10,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Point Lisas and La Romana to US Gulf/Atlantic for the first half of June.

Kerry was open for 12,000 tonnes in bags from south China to Pakistan for similar dates, while Genoc quoted for 14,000 tonnes in bulk from Cuba to Mediterranean with options of Black Sea and Baltic for mid-June.
Express Sea Transport entered the market with an inquiry for 25,000 tonnes of Cuban raws to Egypt, Black Sea or Baltic for mid-June.

E D & F Man was active with new orders, quoting for 12,600 tonnes of bulk sugar from south Brazil to one or two Algerian ports for mid-June and another 11,000 from Thailand to the Philippines for the first half of June.

Shipbrokers said Man also fixed 12,600/15,400 tonnes of bulk sugar from Puerto Quetzal to Algeria for the end of May and a prompt 6,000-tonne bagged cargo from Durban to Dar es Salaam/Mombasa. No rates were given.

CSR was said to have fixed its recent order for 20,000 tonnes min/max bulk sugar from Queensland to Surabaya for June 1/10 and Jean Lion fixed 13/13,500 tonnes, again in bulk, from Thailand to south China.
